method.estimator: SUPERcop stabilized quartiles (stq_longlong); Q2 is primary
method.correctness: SUPERcop try passed in every successful run

compiler_selection.note: These are the per-implementation choices selected by the SUPERcop compile/measure flow, not a forced equal-flag comparison.

candidate_contract.keypair: progressive-P SoA BaseInv/BM plus D2 half-native Q24
candidate_contract.enc: typed private-SoA general B3 plus high-range Q24 pack
candidate_contract.dec: Q24 decode plus global M-native inverse candidate

interpretation.formal_result: Encapsulation and decapsulation are small GT32 wins under the requested SUPERcop method; key generation remains a small loss.
interpretation.encapsulation: The two N5 Forward calls and general B3 saving exceed the remaining decode, r-hat serialization, ciphertext serialization, and glue debts. Older phase attribution remains diagnostic only because it used a different binary and harness.
interpretation.decapsulation: The global M-native inverse removes enough first-product edge work for Q24 and recovered-r boundary savings to exceed the remaining GT-unpack and critical-path debt. The formal margin is only about 40 cycles.
interpretation.keypair: The progressive-P candidate retires less arithmetic/serialization work in earlier PMU studies but uses more loads; BaseInv-to-consumer delivery, the second multiplication, and key serialization return the Forward saving. The direct AoS J1/R1-U route is not selected because it was substantially slower in its native gate.
interpretation.promotion_warning: The margins are below 0.5%. Treat this as a formal same-host SUPERcop result, not a portable claim across CPUs, toolchains, or code placement.
